implementation_notes: ScalaMock ships a dedicated Stubs API: stub[T] macro-generates an implementation of the trait, and warehouse.hasInventory.returnsWith(false) - or .returns(...) when the answer depends on arguments, .returnsOnCall(n, ...) for sequences - programmes the canned value. Calls and times are available but need not be used, which is exactly what distinguishes this from the mock API (mock[T] with expects(...).returning(...)); stub fixtures belong inside each test case, and resetStubs() exists only for the shared-fixture case. The generated stub replaces an anonymous class implementing the trait by hand, which stays a reasonable no-dependency alternative for one or two answers; the framework earns its place through call recording, argument matchers and the effect-system integrations (Future/ZIO/cats-effect).
code_sketch:
class OrderSpec extends AnyFunSuite, Matchers, Stubs:
  test("reports out of stock"):
    val warehouse = stub[Warehouse]
    warehouse.hasInventory.returnsWith(false)

    Order("Talisker", 50).fill(warehouse) shouldBe false
pitfalls: stub[T] must be bound as Stub[T] when the value is passed through a fixture type, otherwise the returnsWith/returns helpers are not available at compile time.
returnsWith ignores arguments while returns matches them; using returnsWith where the SUT passes unexpected arguments hides a bug instead of failing.
Stubs are per test case by default; sharing them across cases (or running cases in parallel) requires resetStubs() and sequential execution.

variants.name: Anonymous trait implementation with canned returns
variants.implementation_notes: Scala traits can be implemented anonymously in place, so the classic structure is one expression: val warehouse = new Warehouse { def hasInventory(sku: String, qty: Int) = false }. The compiler checks the members, no library or macro is involved, and the canned answer is visible where the test uses it. It is the right default for a one- or two-method collaborator, for codebases that keep test dependencies minimal, and for Scala 2/3 code shared with effect systems where a stub layer would need extra wiring; the cost is that multi-method traits must be fully implemented and there is no recording or argument matching - switch to ScalaMock for that.
variants.code_sketch:
val warehouse = new Warehouse:
  def hasInventory(sku: String, qty: Int): Boolean = false

assert(!Order("Talisker", 50).fill(warehouse))
pitfalls: All abstract members must be implemented; give wide traits default implementations or split them at the consumer so the anonymous stub stays small.
Name clashes in the enclosing scope (e.g. the function argument name sku) cause surprising self-references; name the stub's parameters distinctly.
An anonymous stub that closes over mutable test state makes test order significant; keep captured state read-only or rebuild the stub per test.
